clue.text: Photographer has similar facility to that of 17

definitions.meaning: Lord ..., Antony Armstrong-Jones, was a celebrated royal photographer
17 is the Isle of Man peak with a mountain railway; the Welsh peak also has a rack railway to its summit

explanation.surface: A cameraman is said to enjoy the same amenity as whoever owns some other numbered item.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are proper names: the Earl of Snowdon, and the highest mountain in Wales, whose summit railway matches Snaefell's on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Snowdon was a famous society photographer, married to Princess Margaret, so the title names him.

clue.text: One who criticises celebrity chef

definitions.meaning: to slate is to criticise harshly
Nigel ... is a well-known British food writer and television cook

explanation.surface: A famous cook who also hands out harsh reviews.
explanation.definitionFit: Slating means savage criticism, and Nigel Slater is a British TV cook, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Bird rings before end of the day

parts.note: rings are round like the letter O, so several are O's
pre is the Latin prefix meaning before

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here taken from day

explanation.surface: A bird ringed by ornithologists before the day closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes the last letter of 'day'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fish-eating hawk is a large bird of prey, a straightforward example of the category.

clue.text: Events over two days have not clashed badly

indicators.note: something done badly is messed up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Two-day athletics meetings have gone off without clashing too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges NOT CLASHED; 'have' only links definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-event athletics contest is held over two consecutive days, so these are two-day events.

clue.text: Long-distance runner tearing about with no little thanks

indicators.note: about here means turned around and mixed up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
no here means without, so the thanks letters are dropped from the word tearing

parts.note: ta is a short, informal British word for thanks

explanation.surface: A distance athlete races about, too busy to say a quick thank-you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes TA from TEARING, leaving ERING, which 'about' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a crossword runner, and this West African river runs over four thousand kilometres.

clue.text: Attack weapon used by Thatcher to start afresh

indicators.note: starting afresh means the first letter is swapped for a new one

parts.note: Margaret Thatcher's handbag was famous, and 'handbagging' became slang for her verbal attacks

explanation.surface: A weapon the Prime Minister wielded when she wanted a fresh start.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Thatcher's handbag was her legendary weapon; give it a new first letter, S, and it becomes a cosh.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag filled with sand makes a crude cosh, used to strike someone down.

clue.text: Explanations get souls into trouble

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so the letters of the two words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Accounts of events that land people's souls in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' is the anagram signal, working on SOULS and INTO together; 'get' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Answers to problems are explanations of how they work out, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Tip for winning card game

definitions.meaning: in horse racing, a tipster's most confident selection of the day is called a ...
a trick-taking card game, short for Napoleon

explanation.surface: Advice on how to win at cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing tipsters name their surest bet as the nap, and Napoleon (nap) is a card game.

clue.text: Virus supports ongoing problems

parts.note: a bug is an informal word for a virus or infection
bears means holds up or supports

explanation.surface: A lingering infection keeps causing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistent sources of annoyance or worry are pet hates or recurring problems.

clue.text: Fall for the ending of 10 — frequently it can be told

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its tail, so the front of 10 across is dropped and its last three letters kept

parts.note: 10 across is the island group in the Pacific
oft is an old word for often
a story is something that can be told, and a story goes on

explanation.surface: Falling for the end of a tale that is often told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ending of' keeps the closing GOS of 10 across. ON for 'it can be told' is loose: a story told goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall for someone is to become soft-hearted toward them, an idiom of indulgence.

clue.text: A form of stock illustration tacked onto articles

indicators.note: tacked onto means joined on after, so the picture follows the articles

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, so more than one gives a's
pic is short for picture

explanation.surface: An illustration of soup stock is pinned to some articles.
explanation.definitionFit: Savoury jelly is made by setting clarified meat stock, so it is a form of stock.

clue.text: Unique group celebrations securing leading place in the past

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the celebrations wrap around the other pieces

parts.note: galas are festive celebrations

indicators.note: leading means the front letter of place

parts.note: ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A one-of-a-kind group held parties that once secured a top spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unique group' hints at the islands' one-off wildlife, which inspired Darwin.
explanation.definitionFit: These Pacific islands are a unique archipelago, famous for wildlife found nowhere else.

clue.text: German ruler once took in voters

parts.note: an Elector was one of the princes who chose the Holy Roman Emperor
ate means took food in

explanation.surface: A former German prince who absorbed the voters.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole body of people entitled to vote in an election is the electorate.

clue.text: One who was bound to come back in 16

indicators.note: coming back means going the other way, so the letters are read backwards
in means the letters sit inside the answer to 16 down

explanation.surface: A man who was obliged to return to the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' takes FRES from inside ALFRESCO (16 down); 'to come back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval labourer was bound to his lord's land and could not leave it.

clue.text: Dignified way to get queue shortened on a weekday

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
Tues is the short form of Tuesday

indicators.note: shortened means cut down, so the word loses its last letters

parts.note: taken as written, a line of people waiting

explanation.surface: A stately way to cut short the queue on a Tuesday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortened' takes UE off QUEUE to give QUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tall and graceful with a stately bearing looks like a statue, hence dignified.

clue.text: Get an irate look from the last in the chain of five

definitions.text: the last in the chain of five

indicators.note: get here means produce by reworking, so these letters are rearranged into new words

explanation.surface: Someone receives an angry glare from the last person in a line of five.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the five Great Lakes, linked in a chain, this is the most easterly, the last before the St Lawrence.

clue.text: I've got a gal here in Michigan

definitions.text: I've got a gal here in Michigan

parts.words: I've got a gal here in Michigan
parts.note: the Glenn Miller hit is titled I've Got a Gal In ..., naming this Michigan city

explanation.surface: A man boasting of a girlfriend in the Midwest.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1942 song places the singer's sweetheart in this Michigan city, so the clue's line points to it.

clue.text: Outside firm after a large return for 12

indicators.note: after places the firm at the end

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: 12 across is the bound labourer
Co is short for company, a firm

explanation.surface: An outside business follows a big comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in the open air, as with a meal eaten outside.

clue.text: Manly height can be got up on track

definitions.meaning: the highest mountain on the Isle of Man, whose people are Manx

definitions.text: can be got up on track
definitions.meaning: a mountain railway climbs to the summit of this peak

explanation.surface: A tall masculine figure who can be reached by running track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manly' means 'of the Isle of Man', a British Crown dependency in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: This peak is the island's summit, reachable by the Manx electric mountain railway.

clue.text: Little room for dressing containing girdle

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the dressing wraps around the girdle word

parts.note: lint is a soft fabric used to dress wounds
to girdle is to encircle or enclose

explanation.surface: A small dressing room holding a corset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' and 'girdle' both pretend to be clothing; one is a wound dressing, the other a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard for storing sheets and towels is a small storage space, a little room.

clue.text: Fly in Thailand direction, twice

indicators.note: twice means the pair of pieces is written two times

parts.note: T is the international vehicle code for Thailand
SE is south-east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: An insect flying around in Thailand, in one direction and then back.
explanation.definitionFit: An African biting insect that spreads sleeping sickness is a kind of fly.

clue.text: Wit especially getting slower

parts.note: rit, short for ritardando, is the musical direction to slow down

explanation.surface: Humour that is mostly slowing down.
explanation.definitionFit: Liveliness of mind and quickness of humour are what the French borrowing names.

clue.text: Bird said to be back

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word for back is pronounced

parts.note: rear means back

explanation.surface: A bird is reported to have returned.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the two words are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A large flightless South American bird, related to the ostrich.

clue.text: Man with an issue to resolve records what's said

indicators.note: resolving untangles and reshapes, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man with a problem to sort out writes down what's said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to resolve' rearranges MAN and AN ISSUE; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretary taking dictation writes down spoken words, so the clue's phrase describes this scribe.

clue.text: "Fashionable" Med resort said to be a relative term

indicators.note: said means spoken aloud, so the resort's name is heard

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera; nice also means fashionable

explanation.surface: A smart Mediterranean holiday spot is called a family word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashionable' hints at nice, which is also the Riviera city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member, so the word is a kinship term.

clue.text: Female spy sleep-in causes a rumpus

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

indicators.note: in means the sleep letters go inside the spy

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
zz is the comic-strip sign for sleep

explanation.surface: A woman agent's lie-in causes uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: The '-in' of 'sleep-in' is the container signal, so the hyphenated word splits in two jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yiddish-derived word for a noisy muddle or uproar, the same as a rumpus.

clue.text: Have leaders of the opposition waiting nervously

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters, taken from three words

explanation.surface: The opposition's top people nervously wait to have their say.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to hold it as property, the plain sense of the verb.

clue.text: Drug ends drear state

parts.note: qat, or khat, is a stimulant leaf chewed in Arabia and East Africa

indicators.note: ends means only the closing letters of drear are kept

explanation.surface: Drug use ends a dreary situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' keeps only AR, the end of 'drear'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gulf nation is an independent country, which is the sense of state here.

clue.text: Ronaldo playing for US city

indicators.note: playing suggests a footballer moving around, so the name's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The footballer Ronaldo turns out for an American team.
explanation.definitionFit: A Florida city famous for its theme parks, so a US city.

clue.text: Opening partner remains in top place

parts.note: Eve was Adam's partner in the opening book of the Bible, the first woman
the rest is what remains

explanation.surface: An opening batsman's partner stays at the top of the order.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's highest mountain is literally the top place on Earth.
